bands.label: US cuts announced
bands.summary: US media report Washington plans to pull fighter jets, warships and long range strike assets assigned to NATO in Europe while German and NATO voices warn Russia could be ready to attack the alliance by 2029.

bands.label: Posture review
bands.summary: The second Trump administration reviews US global force posture and signals a shift of weight away from Europe while UK and European capitals debate defense spending hikes ahead of the NATO summit.

bands.label: Full scale war era
bands.summary: Russia's invasion of Ukraine triggers the largest NATO reinforcement of Europe since the Cold War, with US air, naval and deep strike assets surged forward to the eastern flank.

bands.label: Post Crimea buildup
bands.summary: After Russia's annexation of Crimea and intervention in eastern Ukraine, NATO rotates enhanced forward presence battlegroups into the Baltics and Poland.

bands.label: Post Cold War expansion
bands.summary: After the Soviet collapse NATO expands eastward through several enlargement rounds while Moscow argues the new security order ignores Russian interests.

frames.label: Jun 2026 announcement
frames.note: The story begins this week with US officials signaling cuts to air, naval and deep strike assets assigned to NATO in Europe. Under this frame it reads as a US force posture decision driven by other theater priorities, with NATO partners reacting. This is the frame the Trump administration and US media outlets reporting the plan open with.

frames.label: Feb 2022 invasion
frames.note: The story begins with Russia's full scale invasion of Ukraine and the NATO buildup that followed. Under this frame the 2026 US cuts read as a reversal mid conflict that leaves Europe more exposed just as the German army chief and NATO members converge on a 2029 threat horizon. This is the frame European defense planners and NATO command voices open with.

frames.label: Post 1991 NATO expansion
frames.note: The story begins with NATO's eastward expansion after the Soviet collapse and what Moscow calls a security architecture that ignored Russia's interests. Under this frame current US troop moves, Arctic activity and 2029 warnings read as the latest cycle of an unresolved 1990s settlement. This is the frame the Russian foreign ministry and TASS commentary open with.
